newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt rejects French bid for cement company.
newsitem.headline: Egypt rejects French bid for cement company.

text.p: Egypt rejected a French bid for a strategic stake in Amriyah Cement because French firm Lafarge was the only competitor, Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said in remarks published on Tuesday.

Obeid, the minister in charge of Egypt's privatisation programme, told reporters on Monday that the state would instead sell its 66 percent stake in the company by auction in tranches on the Egyptian stock exchange, starting within days.

Government newspapers quoted Obeid as saying the French building materials producer had offered to buy 51 percent of Amriyah's 20 million shares for 530 million pounds ($159 million), the equivalent of about 52.00 pounds a share. The shares have since risen to about 62.00 pounds.

"It became clear that a single bid did not give enough of a chance for competition and the bid came after Lafarge had reached an agreement of intentions with an Egyptian party. A dispute broke out and the Egyptian party objected to Lafarge negotiating alone," al-Akhbar quoted Obeid as saying.
Obeid added that the French company had indicated it expected Amriyah Cement to pay 30 million pounds for unspecified services, the newspapers said.
He said a first tranche of between 10 and 14 percent of the Amriyah shares would go on offer in two days.
Egypt first invited one or more strategic international investors to buy at least 40 percent of Amriyah back in May as a step towards full privatisation of the Alexandria company.
It extended the deadline for bids but the offer seemed to have gone further than many other of the state's attempt to find anchor investors for its companies.
